findings.title: Password lockout can be bypassed by sending wrong-password attempts in parallel (school and console sign-in)
findings.what: signIn reads user.failedAttempts when it looks up the login (lookUpLogins, line 113), runs the slow Argon2 check, and then writes the absolute value `failedAttempts: user.failedAttempts + 1` (lines 142-147). It does not use an atomic increment. N requests sent at the same moment all read the same count, so they all write count+1 and the 5-try lock never triggers. consoleSignIn (src/lib/console/auth.ts:132-137) has the same read-then-write pattern. The only remaining limit is the per-IP limit (sign-in:ip, 30 per 10 min; console-sign-in, 30 per 15 min), so the number of guesses per login grows with the number of IPs the attacker has.
findings.proof: Source trace: sign-in.ts:113 lookUpLogins -> :132 lock check on the stale row -> :139 verifyPassword (Argon2id, m=19456, t=2, so slow enough to open a wide race window) -> :144-147 prisma.userLogin.update data.failedAttempts = user.failedAttempts + 1 (stale value). Compare two-step.ts:250 and console/auth.ts:192, which do use `{ increment: 1 }` for code attempts. Not tested live; the parallel burst was not run because it would lock a demo login the QA loop is using.
findings.impact: Someone who knows or guesses a staff username, or the console mobile number, can try many more than 5 passwords per 15 minutes against one login. For the console (DREAM TEAM, every school), a guessed password still needs the second-step code. School logins whose role does not need two-step are fully exposed.
findings.fix: Count failures in one atomic statement, for example `UPDATE user_login SET failed_attempts = failed_attempts + 1, locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_attempts + 1 >= 5 THEN now() + interval '15 min' END WHERE id = $1 RETURNING failed_attempts`, and decide the lock from the returned value. Or add a per-login hitLimit (for example `sign-in:login:<id>`, 5 per 15 min) before verifyPassword, since hitLimit's upsert is already atomic. Do the same in consoleSignIn.

findings.title: Console one-time code check has no rate limit, so its 5-try limit can be raced
findings.what: checkConsoleCode reads c.attempts (line 182) and only then compares the code and increments. Unlike the school verifyChallenge (two-step.ts:242, which has `two-step:check:<user>` at 20 per 15 min) and unlike the welcome finish action (IP limit), the console sign-in code step (consoleCodeAction -> finishConsoleSignIn -> checkConsoleCode) has no hitLimit at all. Parallel posts carrying the same sos_console_step challenge all pass the `attempts >= 5` check before any increment lands.
findings.proof: src/app/console/sign-in/actions.ts:31-40 consoleCodeAction calls finishConsoleSignIn with no hitLimit; console/auth.ts:177-197 checkConsoleCode: findUnique -> `if (c.attempts >= MAX_CODE_TRIES)` on the stale row -> timingSafeEqual -> increment. Every send (5 per 15 min per user) makes a fresh challenge to race. Source only, not executed.
findings.impact: Someone who already has a console password (see the lockout finding) can try far more than 5 of the 1,000,000 codes per challenge, which weakens the second step that guards the DREAM TEAM console (all schools, support access, billing).
findings.fix: Add `hitLimit("console-code-check:<userId>", 20, 900)` and an IP limit before the compare, as verifyChallenge does. Better, make the try count atomic: `UPDATE console_code SET attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE id = $1 AND attempts < 5 AND used_at IS NULL RETURNING attempts`, and refuse when no row comes back.

findings.title: A Staff & HR 'Reset password' link does not sign the person out elsewhere or forget remembered devices
findings.what: Staff & HR 'New sign-in link' (newSignInLink -> issueInvite) is the school's password reset, and it lands on /invite/[token] -> acceptInvite. acceptInvite replaces passwordHash, but it never calls revokeAllSessions or forgetAllDevices, never writes an audit line and never sends a security alert. The blueprint (08-platform-security.md §2, line 28) says remembered devices are forgotten on 'a password change or reset', and changePassword ((school)/actions.ts:141) and the console RESET link (school-invite.ts:103) both revoke sessions. This path does not.
findings.proof: invites.ts:45-69: findInvite -> newPasswordProblem -> keepOldPassword -> userLogin.update(passwordHash, ...), and no session or trustedDevice change. Callers: src/app/invite/[token]/actions.ts:17 only. Reset issued from src/app/(school)/staff-hr-management/[staffId]/actions.ts:205 (issueInvite, which is also called 'Reset password'). grep shows revokeAllSessions is called only from (school)/actions.ts, profile/actions.ts and console/school-invite.ts.
findings.impact: When a staff login is stolen and the school resets it with a sign-in link, the attacker's existing sessions keep working (as long as the school's session rules allow, up to the 30-day cookie) and their remembered device still skips two-step. The reset does not end the takeover, and the owner gets no alert that the password changed.
findings.fix: In acceptInvite, after the update, when the login already had a password (a reset, or the expiry or temporary flow): `await revokeAllSessions(user.id, "Password reset by sign-in link")` (which also forgets devices), write a `changed-password` audit line in each of the login's schools, and send the same securityAlert that changePassword sends. Also make the claim single-use atomically: `updateMany({ where: { id, inviteTokenHash: hashToken(token) }, ... })` and refuse when count is 0.

findings.title: Mobile/email change and switching off two-step need no password re-check, and the old contact is not told
findings.what: sendContactCode / confirmContactCode change the login's phone or email with only a code sent to the NEW value (which the requester controls). setTwoStep(false) switches off self-chosen two-step. Neither asks for the current password, and confirmContactChange (two-step.ts:323-356) only writes an audit line: no securityAlert goes to the old email or phone.
findings.proof: profile/actions.ts:50-76 (requireCurrent only, no password), :78-90 setTwoStep (no password). two-step.ts:344-353 updates phone/email and writes audit only. The new contact is then usable by 'Forgot password? Sign in with a one-time code' (sign-in.ts:304 startCodeSignIn -> findLogin by the new phone/email), which gives a signedInWithCode session that may set a new password without the old one (sessions.ts:458, (school)/actions.ts:123).
findings.impact: Anyone who gets brief use of a signed-in session (a shared staff-room computer, a stolen cookie) can make the takeover permanent: put in their own mobile, switch off two-step, then 'Forgot password' with their own number and set a new password, which signs the real owner out. The owner's old contact gets no warning. This applies to non-two-step roles; two-step roles need both email and phone codes.
findings.fix: Ask for the current password (or a fresh code to the EXISTING contact) before sendContactCode and before setTwoStep(false). After a contact change, send a securityAlert to the OLD email/phone ('Your mobile number on School OS was changed. Not you? ...'). Consider blocking code sign-in to a contact changed in the last 24 hours.

findings.title: On a Vercel 'test copy' the console two-step code is shown on the sign-in page, and the default password is documented
findings.what: testCopyCode returns the code computed from the challenge whenever isTestCopy() is true and no code channel is set up, and console/sign-in/page.tsx:40 renders it (shownCode). isTestCopy() is true on Vercel when neither MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL nor FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set (test-copy-env.ts:19-22). The test copy also seeds demo logins and a console Owner 9849012345 with DEMO_PASSWORD, defaulting to 'SchoolOS@2026', and deploy/vercel/README.md documents both. HANDOFF shows real staff working on the beta deployment.
findings.proof: console/auth.ts:68-75 and :82; console/sign-in/page.tsx:40; test-copy-env.ts:65; scripts/vercel-build.ts:41-48 seeds the demo into an empty database; deploy/vercel/README.md:17-19, 53-58. The live config was not checked (not allowed to contact the live site), so this depends on how the beta is deployed.
findings.impact: If the beta runs as a test copy, console two-step is password-only (the code is on screen). If DEMO_PASSWORD was left as the default, or demo logins still exist next to real school data, anyone who reads the public README can open the console or the demo school-admin logins.
findings.fix: Owner check on the beta's environment variables: confirm FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY / MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL are set (so it is NOT a test copy), and that no demo logins or the 9849012345 console login remain with a known password. In code: refuse to start on a test copy unless DEMO_PASSWORD is set and is not the default, and refuse testCopyCode once any non-demo school exists.

findings.title: With TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=0 every sign-in limit is one shared 'unknown' bucket for the whole platform
findings.what: clientIp returns null when hops <= 0, and every caller then uses the key `...:ip:unknown` (signInAction, codeSignInAction, verifyCodeAction, invite actions, consoleSignIn). All visitors share one counter: 30 password tries per 10 min for the whole platform, after which nobody can sign in with a password until the window ends.
findings.proof: Local build C:/Users/chala/sos-build/.env has TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=0 (read by name and value only, as config). client-ip.ts:8 `if (hops <= 0) return null`; sign-in/actions.ts:63 `sign-in:ip:${device.ipAddress ?? "unknown"}`. The production default (1) behind Vercel is fine; this only bites if 0 is copied to a real deployment.
findings.impact: On a deployment configured with 0, one person sending 30 wrong passwords blocks password sign-in for every school for 10 minutes, and the audit log records no IP.
findings.fix: When the IP is unknown, fall back to a per-login or per-device key rather than one global bucket, and write in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md that TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS must be 1 on Vercel.

finders.covered: Read and found fine: session tokens (32 random bytes, only a SHA-256 hash stored, new token at every sign-in so no session fixation; httpOnly, Secure in production, SameSite=Lax; console cookie SameSite=Strict, path /console); findSession applies the school's idle and longest-sign-in rules on the server and refuses DISABLED or archived logins; sign out, sign out on another device, sign out everywhere and password change revoke sessions and forget remembered devices; remembered-device tokens are tied to the login and cleared by a two-step reset. Two-step codes: randomInt, hashed with their challenge token, 10-minute expiry, timingSafeEqual, used once (updateMany usedAt), earlier codes ended on resend, a per-user check limit of 20 per 15 min, 5 sends per 15 min. The 'Forgot password' code sign-in uses decoy tokens so it gives no enumeration; roles that need two-step need email AND phone codes; a code sign-in never makes a remembered device; a reset without the old password works only within 30 minutes of a code sign-in and only once. Shared phone/email sign-in skips locked logins and has a per-contact limit. A temporary or expired password leads to the first-change page and never to a session. The console School Admin invite needs the link plus an SMS code and the claim is atomic; a RESET revokes sessions. The console welcome link checks the code belongs to the same user. switchSchool's back= redirect is limited to same-site paths, and the sign-in pages take no next= parameter. The support cookie is look-only through the proxy stamp. Not done: the live black-box race tests (to avoid locking demo logins the QA loop is using), Settings Users invite internals and parent/guardian link tokens (other agents).

findings.title: 'Sign in with a one-time code' tells a stranger which mobile numbers, emails or usernames belong to Principal / School Admin logins
findings.what: The owner decided on 2026-11-12 that a login that does not exist must get the same code page as a real one, so nobody can find out which logins exist (see the comment at src/app/sign-in/actions.ts:103-105). codeSignInAction only hides CANNOT_SEND, though. Any other message from startCodeSignIn is shown on the sign-in page. When the typed login is real, active and has a role that needs two-step login (Principal, School Admin and the like), but codes cannot reach both its email and its mobile, startCodeSignIn returns CODE_ALONE_WORDS (line 315). A made-up name gets the decoy code page instead. Tonight's diff (7f50bf70) reworded this message to 'Your login does not have both yet', which says even more clearly that the login exists. The check itself was already there before acbbab5c, so this is not new tonight, but the earlier audits never reported it. The same leak exists in the `started.unreachable` branch (line 318): unreachableWords() says, for example, 'Codes to your mobile go by your school's SMS, which is not set up yet'. On a live server with no dev code log, a real login whose phone cannot get an SMS and which has no email would get that message, while an unknown login gets the decoy page. I have not run this second case on localhost. With SMS being switched off for schools right now (the uncommitted SMS_OFFERED work leaves code SMS on, but most schools have no SMS template), many real logins could fall into it.
findings.proof: Black-box against http://localhost:3000 only, using the script D:/all/Projects/School-OS/qa-output/security/wb-code-enum.mjs (headless Chrome). It opens /sign-in, clicks 'Forgot password? Sign in with a one-time code', types a name and submits. Results: 'nosuchuser-zz91' -> landed on /sign-in/code ('Enter the code', the decoy). 'librarian' (real, no two-step) -> /sign-in/code, the same page. 'principal' -> stayed on /sign-in with role=alert 'For your safety, you need two codes to sign in without your password: one on your mobile and one by email. Your login does not have both yet...'. 'admin' -> the same alert. Code path: actions.ts:102 startCodeSignIn -> sign-in.ts:313-315 needsTwoStepInAny && (!can.email || !can.phone) -> CODE_ALONE_WORDS -> actions.ts:105 `if (!started.ok && started.message !== CANNOT_SEND) return { message: ... }`, so the decoy is skipped.
findings.impact: Anyone on the internet can type mobile numbers or names and learn which ones are a school's Principal or School Admin logins, the highest-value accounts. They are rate limited to 10 tries per IP every 10 minutes, so this takes many addresses but is not stopped. Those confirmed numbers then become targets for password guessing, SIM swap, or WhatsApp phishing that pretends to be DREAM TEAM support. Through the 'unreachable' branch, the same can apply to ordinary staff logins.
findings.fix: In codeSignInAction, send every refusal that depends on the login (CODE_ALONE_WORDS, any `unreachable` result, and BUSY from the per-login send limit) down the same decoy path as CANNOT_SEND: keepChallenge(newDecoyToken()) and redirect to /sign-in/code. If the person still needs the 'two codes' help, show it in the code-page wording for every login, real or not. The answer must not depend on whether the login exists. Add a test that compares the response for an unknown login and for a two-step login with only one contact.

finders.covered:
I read the whole diff acbbab5c..HEAD for src (153 files, about 4,000 lines without the i18n catalogues), file by file. I also checked the uncommitted work in progress in the working tree, which a running build may include. That covers the messaging libraries, parent-link, admission, front-office and settings, plus the server actions. I found no security regression tonight. What I checked and found sound:

- **Guardian edit `?student=`** (guardians/[id]/edit/page.tsx). It is checked against a UUID regex. It is used only for the back link, Cancel and the redirect after saving. On the edit path, saveGuardianAction(id, from) still runs studentAction("edit", manage) and visibleGuardian, and only creates a link when guardianId is null, which was already the case before. The new 'Change phone or name' link on the child profile only shows when can.manage is true.
- **'Add my staff record' link `/staff-hr-management/add?login=<own userId>`.** The add page already had the `login` parameter: it is checked against the UUID regex and goes through linkableLogin with the viewer's campus. Logins made from Staff & HR still go through loginGrantRefusal (login-ceiling.ts).
- **New default posts with defaultRoleKey principal / school-admin** (staff/settings.ts). These only seed new schools. Add Staff and staff import both reach createStaff -> loginGrantRefusal, which blocks giving a top role unless the person can change Settings, Users & Permissions. guessRole already mapped 'principal' before.
- **Employment campusId made optional.** saveEmployment still runs campusAllows / offCampus for one-campus viewers. updateStaffSection drops a blank campusId, so it keeps the existing one.
- **createYear auto-ACTIVE.** There is still one active year per campus, enforced by the unique index academic_year_one_active, and an audit entry is written. The only problem is that the flash in createYearAction still says 'It is Upcoming until you open it', which contradicts the new behaviour. That is a wording bug, not a security one.
- **Add-student Aadhaar made optional.** It is still nulled unless can.seeRestricted. The edit path is unchanged.
- **Fee head bankAccountId and admission class fee are kept when their field is hidden** (fd.has checks). This changes nothing about who can change what.
- **`/approvals/[id]?reject=1`, enquiries `?do=add`, homework `?do=give`, fee dashboard `?fall=1`.** All of these only change what the screen shows. Server actions recheck everything, and none of them builds a redirect URL from user input, so there is no open redirect.
- **New confirm dialogs** (ActButton confirm, refund ApproveButton via ConfirmButton). They call the same server actions, which run their own requireAction and decision checks.
- **Messaging.** The committed planMessage change only alters which reason text is collected; nobody gets messages they should not. The uncommitted SMS_OFFERED work only removes SMS as a channel. One-time codes keep their SMS path: two-step-sms.ts sends with oneTimeCode, so smsAllowed stays true, and codeChannels covers admission and pickup codes. saveRuleAction keeps a rule's saved SMS choice. I found no path that adds recipients or channels.
- **Client imports.** Common-passwords.ts and ui-sound.ts have no server-only imports and hold no secrets. SMS_OFFERED is client-safe on purpose.
- **Dashboard text.** The early-warning, attendance, money and communication widget changes are wording only, on data each widget already had. Approvals page wording ('All requests', 'no one yet') does not change the inbox query. Salary Structures 'next revision' is shown in the same gated column as the current gross.
- **PDF retry.** printWith keeps `javaScriptEnabled: false` on the retry with a fresh browser.
- **One-option SelectField.** It sends the same single allowed value as a hidden input.

The black-box probe was run against localhost:3000 only. My scratch files are in D:/all/Projects/School-OS/qa-output/security/: wb-diff.txt, wb-uncommitted.txt and wb-code-enum.mjs.

findings.title: Time Table print route answers HTTP 500 instead of 403 for roles without Academic Management
findings.what: handleGET calls requireAction("academic-management", "view") without catching PermissionDeniedError (sibling routes such as admit-cards/pdf catch it and return 403). A refused person gets a server error instead of a plain refusal. No data is returned.
findings.proof: GET http://localhost:3000/academic-management/time-table/print with the student, driver and reception sessions -> 500 each time (scratch script qa-output/security/bb/lowrole.mjs, results in lowrole-teacher-student-driver-reception.json). The same roles get 403 or a /no-access redirect on every other out-of-role route.
findings.impact: No data leaks. A refusal shows up as a server error, which fills the error logs and alerts, and the person gets no clear message.
findings.fix: Wrap requireAction in try/catch as in examination-results/admit-cards/pdf/route.ts: return new Response(e.message, {status: 403}) when e is a PermissionDeniedError.

findings.title: previewNoticeResend throws an unhandled error for a notice id from another school
findings.what: When the notice id is not visible to the caller (another school's notice, hidden by RLS), noticeResendInput throws and the server action fails with an error digest instead of returning {ok:false, message}. Nothing of the other school is shown.
findings.proof: POST /dashboard with the header Next-Action set to the previewNoticeResend id, body ["e9a2942a-800a-4406-b238-664660d2dcce","sms"] (a Sunrise notice), sent with the Day One admin session -> 200 with body '1:E{"digest":"1636166234"}'. The same call as the Sunrise admin -> {ok:false, message:"Every parent has seen this notice..."}.
findings.impact: Hardening only. The other school's notice is not disclosed, but an unknown id produces server errors.
findings.fix: Catch the not-found error in previewNoticeResend (the try block exists, so map that error kind) and return {ok:false, message:'This notice was not found.'}.

findings.title: Admit-card and report-card PDF routes check the input before checking the person's permission
findings.what: The UUID check runs before requireAction, so roles without Examination Results (student, driver, reception) get 400 'Choose the exam and the class first.' instead of 403. The report-cards/pdf route behaves the same way. With valid-looking ids the permission check runs afterwards and refuses, so nothing leaks.
findings.proof: GET /examination-results/admit-cards/pdf and /examination-results/report-cards/pdf with the student, driver and reception sessions, no query -> 400 with the input message (lowrole.mjs). Source lines 24-28: the UUID test comes before requireAction.
findings.impact: Information only. A refused role learns the route's expected inputs; it gets no data.
findings.fix: Call requireAction first, then check the input.

finders.covered:
Black-box only, all against http://localhost:3000. Scripts are in D:/all/Projects/School-OS/qa-output/security/bb/ (h.mjs, unauth.mjs, lowrole.mjs, harvest.mjs, cross.mjs, act.mjs, a1.mjs, a2.mjs); JSON results are next to them.

1) Unauthenticated: 511 requests covering all 190 route handlers and all 322 pages, with dummy ids. 422 redirected to /sign-in, 50 got 401, the rest got 403/404/405/400. The only 200s were public pages (sign-in, apply, invite, verify, Parent Link and pay links) showing 'link does not work' text for dummy tokens, /api/v1/health, the driver manifest, and /api/v1/jobs/tick. jobs/tick runs background jobs without a login, but by design: it takes no input, returns no data and is rate-limited.

2) Low roles (teacher, student, driver, reception): 921 requests to every non-id route and page of modules their role marks '-' in 05-roles.md (fees, finance, salary, settings, audit log, data export, inventory, hostel and others). Every one got 403, a 307 to /no-access, or a streamed /no-access redirect. The one exception is /inventory-management/report-problem, which every staff role and the student can open; it looks intended. Direct server-action call: searchStudents as student and driver -> no-permission error; as teacher -> only the teacher's own class student. Class scoping holds.

3) Cross-school: harvested 124 URL patterns, about 240 real Sunrise record URLs (students, guardians, staff, payments with receipt and tax-invoice, fee ledger and its export, approvals, notices, templates, surveys, events, albums, datesheets, marks, inventory, library, transport routes, users and roles, exits and offer letters, imports and switching) and requested them all with the Day One admin session. Every one got 404 or a not-found page. Receipts give PDFs to the Sunrise admin and 404 to Day One. The only 200s were signed bearer links (/g/ album token and /api/v1/files with an HMAC signature), which work without any login by design. Server actions as Day One with Sunrise ids: studentsInSection -> [], findRecords -> [], previewResend -> not found, previewNoticeResend -> error but nothing disclosed (finding 2). Document-design preview PDFs with ?student= or ?staff= set to a Sunrise id, as Day One: the file is byte-for-byte the same size as Day One's own sample preview (57351 B and 73406 B), while the Sunrise admin's file differs. Isolation holds.

Not done: the reverse direction (Day One ids used from Sunrise; only 14 Day One URL patterns exist), query-parameter tampering for other campuses (campus=, year=, student=), and direct calls to the sensitive write actions (settings users, fee payments, salary). A safety check stopped the session before those calls, so they need a separate pass. Past fixes confirmed by these tests: cross-school RLS on pages, receipts and design previews; low-role refusals on module pages and route handlers.

findings.title: Staff & HR can give a login roles with more access than the giver holds (HR makes itself an Accountant or Vice Principal)
findings.what: loginGrantRefusal() only refuses top roles (School Admin, Principal, any role that opens Settings) and personal exceptions above the giver's own level. It never compares a chosen ROLE's permissions with the giver's own permissions. So a person with Staff & HR Full but no Fee, Finance or Salary rights (the HR template: staff-hr Full, salary View, fee and finance none) can give any non-top role, such as Accountant (Fee Full, Finance Full, Salary Full) or the Vice Principal template (Full on Students, Academic, Attendance, Exams, Homework, Events), to a login whose password they set. The file's own rule says 'You can give a login only the access you have yourself', but that is enforced for exceptions only.
findings.proof: Source path: Add Staff (src/app/(school)/staff-hr-management/add/actions.ts createStaffAction) or giveLoginAction ([staffId]/actions.ts:173) -> giveLogin (src/lib/staff/staff.ts:276). At staff.ts:283 the only check is loginGrantRefusal(granterOf(...), roles, login.exceptions). In login-ceiling.ts:73-85 roles are checked only with roles.some(isTopRole). isTopRole (line 67) is true only for school-admin, principal, or settings != none. Accountant's settings mark is '-' (src/lib/roles.ts READY_ROLES accountant column ends in '-'), so it passes. With signIn=password, giveLogin creates the login ACTIVE with HR's typed temporary password (staff.ts ~line 308) and copies phone and email from the staff record HR just typed (staff.ts:305), so the Accountant role's two-step code also goes to an address HR chose. Steps: an HR login adds a staff member 'X' with HR's own email, ticks Give login, role Accountant, temporary password P, then signs in as X and gets the two-step code by email -> full Fee, Finance and Salary Management. The only control is the alert to School Admins (alertPermissionChange), which is after the fact.
findings.impact: An HR person (or any role with Staff & HR Full that cannot manage users) gains fee collection and cancellation, the Day Book, expenses and salary approval in their school, or Vice Principal powers, by creating a login for a made-up staff member.
findings.fix: In loginGrantRefusal, when !managesUsers(g), also refuse any role whose permission level in any module is above the giver's own (compare LEVEL[role.permissions[m]] with g.permissions[m] for see and change, as already done for exceptions), with LOGIN_CEILING_WORDS.above and field 'roleKeys'. Apply the same check in the staff import path that gives logins.

findings.title: Staff & HR 'New sign-in link' (password reset) works for logins with more access than the person resetting, and the link is shown to them: account takeover
findings.what: signInLinkRefusal() refuses a reset only for top roles the giver does not hold, for personal exceptions the giver could not give, and for logins that open another school. It does not check the target's ROLES against the giver's access, although its own words (LOGIN_CEILING_WORDS.linkAbove: 'a login with access to Settings or more access than yours') say it should. newSignInLink then returns the invite link to the HR browser.
findings.proof: src/app/(school)/staff-hr-management/[staffId]/actions.ts:193-207: who(fd, hrOnly=true) needs Staff & HR change 'all'; heldHere() reads the target's roles; signInLinkRefusal(granterOf, held.roles, {exceptions, elsewhere}); then issueInvite() and `return { link, username, sent }`. The staff act() wrapper (src/lib/staff/act.ts:47-54) returns { ok, message, data: result }, so the /invite/<token> link reaches the HR screen. acceptInvite (src/lib/auth/invites.ts:45-69) sets the new password with only the token, no code. Steps: HR opens the staff record of a Vice Principal, Office Staff, Exam In-charge or Librarian (roles with requiresTwoStep false in src/lib/roles.ts), clicks New sign-in link, opens the returned link, sets a password, signs in as that person. For Accountant targets the two-step code still goes to the victim, which blocks it; roles without two-step are open.
findings.impact: An HR user takes over any non-admin staff login whose role exceeds HR's own (Vice Principal, Office Staff with Admission and Student Full, Exam In-charge), and acts as them (marks, admissions, student records) under their name in the audit log.
findings.fix: In signInLinkRefusal, when !managesUsers(g), return LOGIN_CEILING_WORDS.linkAbove if any target role's level in any module is above g.permissions for that module (same comparison as the exception check). Optionally also send the reset link only to the person's own phone or email and never return it to the screen for logins other than ones HR just created.

findings.title: A School Admin limited to one campus can widen their own access to the whole school, or invite whole-school logins, in Settings, Users & Permissions
findings.what: changeAccess() and inviteUser() accept any scope (WHOLE_SCHOOL, CAMPUS of any campus) from the form and never compare it with the actor's own campus limit (current.campusId). changeAccess also allows the actor's own userLoginId. So a person kept to one campus (scope CAMPUS) with Settings edit can set their own School Access to Whole school, or invite a new School Admin login with whole-school scope to an email they control. 20-settings.md says a one-campus person 'sees and changes only that campus's ... every action'; this removes that limit completely.
findings.proof: src/app/(school)/settings/users/actions.ts:85 accessAction reads userId, roleIds, scope, campusId from the form -> runSettings('users','edit') (only requireSettingsAction: Settings reach 'all' and page mode; no campus check) -> changeAccess (users.ts:182). changeAccess uses checkScope (users.ts:80-88), which only checks that the scope value exists and that a CAMPUS campus exists, and keepOneAdmin; there is no `userLoginId === ctx.userId` refusal and no campus check (grep for 'campus' in settings/users/actions.ts shows only form parsing at lines 31, 62, 89, 91). inviteAction (actions.ts:39) passes parsed.data.scope/campusId straight to inviteUser (users.ts:115), which also calls only checkScope. Steps: a campus-limited School Admin posts accessAction with userId = their own login id, their current roleIds and scope=WHOLE_SCHOOL; the next request's accessIn() gives them whole-school reach. Commit 8777bb36 shows campus-limited School Admins are a supported principal.
findings.impact: A branch (one-campus) School Admin of a multi-campus school reaches every other campus's students, staff, fees and salary, defeating the campus model in one form post.
findings.fix: In changeAccess, inviteUser (and setExceptions, enable/disable, linkRecord) when the actor has current.campusId: refuse a scope other than CAMPUS with that same campusId, refuse acting on a login whose live access is on another campus or whole school, and refuse changing one's own access (as disableUser already does at users.ts:261).

findings.title: Import files (move-in files) are not bound to campus or uploader: a one-campus person can read, download, fix, import and remove another campus's uploaded file
findings.what: forFile() loads the MoveInFile by id with getFile(tx, id) (src/lib/move-in/service.ts:222, where: { id, archivedAt: null }) and checks only placeRefusal (place, role, kind). Neither forFile, placeRefusal (src/lib/imports/place-access.ts), the problems download (src/lib/imports/place-routes.ts:46-56), the import page list (src/components/import/import-home.tsx:41) nor the review page (FileReview) checks the file's campus or who uploaded it. This is the run-3 deferred unit 'Import file write actions on a file chosen by id'; it is still open.
findings.proof: import-home.tsx:41 lists every open file of the place's kinds: tx.moveInFile.findMany({ where: { kind: { in: keys }, status: { in: ['open','importing'] }, archivedAt: null } }), so file ids of every campus are shown with links. placeProblemsResponse (place-routes.ts:52-56) then returns the raw cells of every problem row (student rows include Aadhaar, DOB, parent phones) after only placeRefusal. fixRowAction / chooseRowAction / leaveOutAction / importAction / removeAction (file-actions.ts:290-321) all go through onFile -> forFile with the same checks; importFile (service.ts:608-628) starts the import with the file's stored options (the uploader's section and campus), and removeFile archives it. Steps: a Principal limited to campus B opens Student Management > Import, sees campus A's open file, opens /student-management/import/review/<id>/problems and receives campus A students' rows; or presses Import or Remove on it. Undo is safe: undoImport throws OtherCampusError.
findings.impact: A one-campus Principal or admin (and in the Staff, Salary and Admission places, a one-campus HR, Accountant or counsellor) reads another campus's student or staff rows, Aadhaar included, and can bring in or discard that campus's pending import.
findings.fix: Store the uploader's campus on MoveInFile (or use createdById plus that person's campus) and in forFile, placeProblemsResponse, FileReview and ImportHome refuse or hide a file whose campus is not campusAllows(current, file.campusId); also bind importBatch error downloads (placeErrorsResponse and student-management/import/[batchId]/errors/route.ts) the same way.

findings.title: Settings 'Send invite again' works on a login that also opens another school of the group, and shows the link to the admin: cross-school takeover of a still-invited login
findings.what: resendInvite() checks only belongsHere() (any School Access in this school, ever) and status INVITED, then makes a new invite token; resendInviteAction returns `/invite/<token>` to the School Admin's screen. Unlike updateDetails (users.ts:374) and Staff & HR newSignInLink (elsewhere check), it does not refuse a login that also works in another school. Whoever opens the link sets the one password that opens every school of that login.
findings.proof: src/app/(school)/settings/users/actions.ts:78-82: runSettings('users','edit', resendInvite) then `link: /invite/${r.data.token}`. users.ts:169-179 has no worksElsewhere/schoolsFor check. src/lib/console/schools.ts:431-447 (addAdmin) reuses an existing login in another school of the same Group, so one INVITED login can hold access in two schools. acceptInvite (src/lib/auth/invites.ts:45) needs only the token. Two-step at sign-in (sign-in.ts:195 needsTwoStepInAny) sends the code to the login's own phone or email, so the takeover works when none of the login's roles in any school needs two-step, or the school switched the two-step feature off.
findings.impact: The School Admin of school A can set the password of a group colleague who has not accepted yet and act as them in school B (another tenant), for example as Vice Principal or Teacher there.
findings.fix: In resendInvite, refuse (as updateDetails does) when schoolsFor(userLoginId) includes another school; let only the person, the console, or an admin of every school concerned send it, and send the link only by message instead of returning it to the screen.

findings.title: Import template, problems and skipped-rows downloads skip the paused-school rule
findings.what: placeTemplateResponse, placeProblemsResponse and placeErrorsResponse start with getCurrent() instead of requireCurrent()/requireAction(), so they never apply isPaused(): in a school DREAM TEAM suspended or closed, where requireCurrent sends everyone except the School Admin and Principal to /paused, any login whose role passes placeRefusal can still download import rows (with Aadhaar) and templates with the school's lists.
findings.proof: place-routes.ts:24, 47, 73 call getCurrent(); src/lib/current.ts:157-170 shows the paused redirect lives only in requireCurrent (used by requireAction/requirePage). Every other file route in src/app/(school) goes through requireAction/routeAction and therefore requireCurrent. 22 module import routes plus 3 Settings ones use these helpers.
findings.impact: Staff of a suspended or closed school (for example an Office Staff login with Student Management Full) keep downloading student import rows after access was paused.
findings.fix: Use requireCurrent() (or check isPaused(current) && !pausedAdmin(current) and answer 403) at the start of the three helpers.

finders.covered:
Method: white-box only, no localhost writes, no repo edits. Scratch scripts are in D:/all/Projects/School-OS/qa-output/security/ (wb-enum2.cjs, wb-enum2.txt, wb-routes.txt, wb-byid.txt).

Entry guards, counted:
- 135 "use server" files (112 in (school)) hold 1030 exported functions (942 in (school)). A script matched each export to a guard: requireAction/requireCurrent/requirePage or a module wrapper that calls requireAction (act/actSimple, evAction, feeAction/moneyAction/salaryAction, hwForm/hwQuick/hwAsk, runSettings/requireSettingsAction, studentAction/onStudent, admissionAct, commAction/commOfficeAction, inTransport/trPerson, the lib/{library,hostel,inventory,front-office,reports,events}/act wrappers, staff who()/run()).
- 17 exports had no guard the script could see. I checked each by hand: communication/settings uses a local run() with commAction("edit") plus a full check; staff photo goes through savePhoto -> run -> who(); student saveContact/saveEnrolment/uploadPhoto/addEmergency go through onStudent -> studentAction("edit", manage) + loadVisibleStudent. The rest are public sign-in, invite and apply flows or console actions with their own token or console guards.
- 190 route.ts files (165 under (school)). Every school route has a guard (requireAction/routeAction, evExport, foExport, homeworkExport, hostelRoute/invRoute/libRoute, staffRouteAccess, trPerson, feePdf, placeRefusal helpers, getCurrent plus a permission check).

Wrong permission and module mismatches: I grepped every requireAction/requirePage module against its folder. The cross-module ones (dashboard/profile -> settings edit, inventory -> finance, settings -> student create) are intended. The 13 view-level guards on server actions (reminders, mark seen, acknowledge notice, self review, fee follow-up, clash check, suggestions) were checked. Support look-only staff cannot use them because src/proxy.ts and supportRefusal block every non-GET.

Checked and fine:
- Optional modules: Transport, Library, Hostel and Inventory actions and routes all check modulesOn.
- Salary: own and full levels in slips PDF, generate export, statement, bank file, history report, advances and structures exports, salaryAction "full only", plus campus.
- Exams: marks save/submit/lock bind entry, section and student to teachesPaper and the paper's roster.
- Academic: the act wrapper checks campus via yearOf/campusOf and needs manage/arrange; lesson-plan owner checks.
- Fees: payments cancel/verify/reject/new link/post unmatched use mustSee/canSeeStudent; verify goes through decide().
- Approvals: decide refuses your own request, a request about you, the wrong approver or another campus; one decision only.
- Staff & HR: who() campus check via offCampus; the employment-edit campus fix; class-teacher and allocation sections bound to the staff member's campus year.
- Login linking (link-login.ts): limited to the campus, never a second login. Staff contact edits do not change login phone or email. Settings updateDetails refuses logins shared with another school. Two-step is decided across all of a login's schools. Profile actions are self-only.
- Import undo (undoImport OtherCampusError) still holds.
- Run-3 fixes re-checked and still in place: the login ceiling for top roles, Settings exceptions, exit and the elsewhere check; Settings Own reach refused for changes.

Not covered: per-handler campus filters on every list read (the campus-guard baseline of 197 reads) and the Finance pages for one-campus logins. Both are listed as separate units in run-3.

findings.title: Student 'Generate logins' resets the password of any login linked to the student, including a login that also works in another school or holds School Admin/Principal roles
findings.what: generateLogins() puts a fresh invite (set-password) token on whatever User Login the student record points to (tx.userLogin.update({ where: { id: s.userLoginId }, data: invite })) and returns the /invite/<token> link on screen and in the CSV. Unlike the Staff & HR 'New sign-in link' (newSignInLink in staff-hr-management/[staffId]/actions.ts, which calls heldHere + worksElsewhere + signInLinkRefusal, the run-2 L5 / run-3 fix), it does no check on the login's roles, its status, or whether it opens another school. acceptInvite() (src/lib/auth/invites.ts:44-75) accepts the token for an ACTIVE login and overwrites its password. Settings 'Belongs to' (linkRecord, src/lib/settings/users.ts:335-360) lets a Settings-Full user link ANY login that has access here to a student record, also without checking roles or other schools. So the protection added for shared and top-role logins can be walked around through the student path.
findings.proof: Code path (white-box, not executed, because running it would change a demo login's password that other testers use): 1) School A Principal or School Admin (Settings Full) opens Settings > Users > <group principal's login, which also has School Access in school B> and sets 'Belongs to' = Student X: linkAction -> linkRecord(kind 'student'). The only checks are belongsHere (any School Access row in A) and 'student has no other login'. 2) Student Management > select Student X > Generate logins: loginsAction (student-management/_actions/bulk.ts:103-121) -> generateLogins: because s.userLoginId is set, line 41 updates that login's inviteTokenHash and returns link `${origin}/invite/${token}`. 3) Open /invite/<token>, type a new password: acceptInvite finds the login by inviteTokenHash (no status/role check), sets passwordHash, status ACTIVE. 4) Sign in as that login and switch school (switchSchool lists every school with access) -> full Principal access in school B. Compare newSignInLink, which refuses exactly this case ('or that also opens another school (run-3)').
findings.impact: A Principal or School Admin of one school in a group takes over the shared login of a person who runs another school of the group (cross-school account takeover). Inside one school, anyone with Student Management 'edit, manage' can reset the password of a School Admin or Principal login once that login is linked to a student record, which goes around the rule that top-role passwords are only reset from Settings.
findings.fix: In generateLogins, for an existing s.userLoginId only make a new link when the login is a student login of this school only: refuse (or skip with a reason line) when worksElsewhere(login, ctx.schoolId) is true, when the login holds any role other than the Student role here, or when it is DISABLED or archived. Also make linkRecord refuse kind 'student' for a login that holds a non-student role or works in another school. Better still, route both through the same signInLinkRefusal() check the Staff & HR path uses.

findings.title: With TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=0 every visitor shares one 'unknown' rate-limit bucket, so one anonymous person can block sign-in, receipts, pay links and online admissions for every school
findings.what: clientIp() returns null when TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS is 0 (documented as 'no proxy in front of the app'), and every public limit keys on `${ip ?? "unknown"}`. Every visitor of every school then counts against the same bucket: sign-in:ip:unknown (30 per 10 min, app/sign-in/actions.ts:64), two-step:ip:unknown (30/10 min), code-sign-in:ip:unknown (10/10 min), apply-submit:ip:unknown (5 per hour, lib/admission/public.ts), apply-code (10/h), pay:ip:unknown (30/10 min), receipt-link:ip:unknown (20/10 min), pl-code/pl-verify, invite and school-invite. If hops is 1 with no proxy in front, X-Forwarded-For is taken from the client and can be rotated to skip the limits instead (the code comment says so).
findings.proof: Black-box against http://localhost:3000 (this laptop's .env has TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=0). Script qa-output/security/xff.cjs sent 24 GET /r/<real school hex><payment hex><bad secret> with X-Forwarded-For 203.0.113.7: 404 x19, then 429. It then sent 24 more with a different X-Forwarded-For each time (198.51.100.1..24): all 24 were 429. So the bucket is shared by every address, not per visitor. (Side effect: parent receipt links on the local server were refused for 10 minutes.) I did not run the same on sign-in so that other testers on localhost were not locked out, but sign-in uses the same pattern (sign-in:ip:unknown, 30 per 600 s).
findings.impact: On a host set up with TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=0, one anonymous visitor sending about 30 bad sign-ins every 10 minutes stops every staff member of every school from signing in. Five fake applications an hour close the online admission form for every school, and the same works for parent pay links and receipts. A wrong hop count instead makes the per-IP brute-force limits useless.
findings.fix: Never share one global bucket. When clientIp() is null, skip the per-IP limit and rely on the per-account, per-link and per-phone limits that already exist (sign-in:shared:<contact>, pl-code:link, apply-pay:app...), or use the socket address where the host gives it. Refuse to start in production when TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS is 0, or log a loud warning, and document the right value for each host (Vercel: 1).

findings.title: A School Admin of one school signs a shared login out of every other school, resets its two-step login everywhere, unlocks it and sees its other-school sessions
findings.what: For a User Login that also opens another school: disableUser revokes ALL the login's sessions (tx.session.updateMany({ where: { userLoginId, revokedAt: null } })) and calls forgetAllDevices, including sessions and trusted devices in school B. The Staff & HR exit and switch-off code scopes this to `schoolId: ctx.schoolId` when worksElsewhere is true (lib/staff/exit.ts:261, 344). changeAccess does the same at line 208. resetTwoStep (line 327) sets the global twoStepResetAt, so school B's two-step for that person is reset by school A. enableUser (line 300) clears failedAttempts and lockedUntil globally, which lifts a brute-force lockout. The user page (settings/users/[id]/page.tsx:81) lists the login's live sessions in every school, with IP and device.
findings.proof: Code read. Settings > Users > <shared login> > Disable in school A: disableUser line 271 updateMany has no schoolId filter, and line 272 forgetAllDevices runs even when `others.length > 0` (line 269 only guards the status change). Two-step reset: line 327 updates the userLogin row, which has no row-level security and is shared by every school.
findings.impact: A School Admin of school A can sign a group principal out of school B and remove their trusted devices, weaken their two-step login in school B, unlock a login that was locked after wrong passwords, and see where the person signs in for school B. No data of school B is read.
findings.fix: When worksElsewhere(login, ctx.schoolId) is true: revoke only sessions with schoolId = ctx.schoolId and do not forget devices (as exit.ts does), refuse resetTwoStep and the global unlock in enableUser (send the person to DREAM TEAM or to their own profile), and show only this school's sessions on the user page.

findings.title: Wrong-code counters are read then incremented, so parallel requests get more than 5 guesses per code
findings.what: checkCode reads parentLinkCode.attempts, compares, and then runs `attempts: { increment: 1 }` in a separate step. Requests sent at the same moment all read attempts < 5 before any increment lands. finishSchoolInvite (src/lib/console/school-invite.ts:80-85, the School Admin first-password page /i/[token], which creates a session) has the same read-then-increment pattern.
findings.proof: Code read: links.ts:329-336. `row.attempts >= CODE_TRIES` is checked on the value read; the increment is not conditional (no `where: { attempts: { lt: 5 } }`). Only the per-IP limit (pl-verify 20 per 10 min; school-invite 20 per 10 min) bounds the parallel guesses, and that limit is shared or spoofable as described in the rate-limit finding.
findings.impact: Someone holding a forwarded Parent Link, or a School Admin invite link, gets about 20 or more guesses at the 6-digit code per window instead of 5. The chance of success stays small.
findings.fix: Count the try atomically before comparing: `updateMany({ where: { id: row.id, attempts: { lt: CODE_TRIES }, usedAt: null }, data: { attempts: { increment: 1 } } })` and refuse when count is 0, then compare. Do the same for schoolInvite.codeAttempts.

findings.title: Console WhatsApp webhook passes any unsigned request on to the gym's live site and returns that site's answer
findings.what: POST /api/v1/console/whatsapp calls passOn(raw, headers) before any signature check (route.ts:41-46). It forwards the body and the caller's x-hub-signature-256 header to CONSOLE_WHATSAPP_FORWARD_URL (the gym's site on the shared Meta app) and sends the gym's status and up to 1000 characters of its body back to the anonymous caller as the response.
findings.proof: Code read: route.ts POST: `const passed = await passOn(raw, req.headers); const own = await ownPart(...); return reply(passed ?? own);`. passOn has no verifyMetaSignature call. Locally the forward URL is not set (POST returned 404), so this was not run against the gym's site, which is a shared live setup.
findings.impact: Anyone can use School OS as a relay to post to the gym's webhook and read its replies. That is only safe while the gym's site checks Meta's signature itself.
findings.fix: Forward only after verifyMetaSignature(raw, signature, CONSOLE_WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET) passes. Meta signs with the same app secret for both sites, so unsigned traffic can be dropped. Return a fixed body instead of the gym's text.

finders.covered:
Where I looked and found no problem:

- **Row-level security, checked in the live local database (pg_catalog)**
  - Every one of the 402 tables with school_id has RLS enabled and forced, plus a school_id = app_school_id() policy. No table is missed.
  - The tables without RLS (user_login, session, two_step_challenge, trusted_device, password_history, rate_limit_bucket, error_event, system_notice, backup_run) are the global ones by design.
  - The console tables are gated by app_in_console().
  - school_os_app has no DELETE or TRUNCATE grant, no BYPASSRLS, and is not a member of school_os_owner.
  - The security-definer functions are fixed lookups with set search_path: find_parent_link, admission_school_by_code, verify_certificate (code length 12 to 64), claim_background_jobs, active_school_ids and purge_school (needs console mode and a CLOSED school).
- **Database access in the code**
  - set_config is only ever transaction-local and only in src/lib/db.ts.
  - The $queryRawUnsafe calls are parameterised, or are savepoints or the restore test.
  - Every withSchool with a schoolId from outside the session gets that id from an HMAC-checked token or a definer lookup.
  - switchSchool and getCurrent re-check School Access through withUser.
- **Console**
  - It has its own console_session cookie (path /console, SameSite strict) and the CONSOLE_HOST check.
  - Its actions go through consoleAct or requireConsoleAction.
  - Black-box: /console with a school session returns 307 to /console/sign-in.
  - Support access: one-time ticket, proxy stamp, non-GET refused by src/proxy.ts. withConsoleSchool on the school side is used only for its own Support Access Request and billing rows.
- **Public tokens**
  - File links: HMAC over (file, school, expiry), timing-safe.
    - A swapped school gives 403, another school's file under this school's signature gives 404 (RLS), an expired link gives 410, an empty token gives 403.
    - Archived vault documents are refused on share links.
    - Responses carry nosniff and a CSP sandbox.
  - Pay links: 24 random bytes or an HMAC, stored hashed, expire, rate-limited. confirmCheckout checks the order is bound to the link, the Razorpay signature and capture, and posts once per gateway payment id.
  - Receipt /r/ keys: 132-bit HMAC (a bad key gives 404). The /pay receipt needs a paid link.
  - Parent Link:
    - The token is an HMAC of the link id with a hash lookup.
    - A new phone needs an OTP to the guardian's mobile, with a per-link send limit.
    - Revocation and switches are checked again on every action.
    - Fees, receipts, tax invoices, report cards, events, PTM and consent each check the child belongs to the guardian (assertChild, isChildOfGuardian, childrenOfGuardian, assertGuardianOf).
    - Due ids are filtered to the student's open dues.
  - Apply portal:
    - The school is found by code through the definer function.
    - The status link is an HMAC of school and application.
    - OTP and per-IP limits apply, and the fee checkout is bound to the application.
  - Surveys (HMAC per invite, answered once with a conditional update), albums (HMAC plus version, staff albums refused) and calendar feeds (HMAC plus version, feed switch) are all fine.
  - Invite, /i and first-change tokens are random and hashed, expire, and are cleared on use.
- **Webhooks**
  - Razorpay: HMAC over the raw body with the gateway's own secret, looked up inside the school's RLS.
  - WhatsApp: Meta signature with the school's app secret, filtered to the school's own phone_number_id. The verify token is compared timing-safe.
  - MSG91: key compared timing-safe.
  - Console WhatsApp and console Razorpay: env secret. The console Razorpay route says "not set up" before any signature work.
  - Black-box: bad or missing signatures gave 401/403/404.
- **Other APIs**
  - The attendance device API uses a hashed key looked up per school.
  - The driver API refuses calls without auth.
  - push/open is bound to the notification's own user.
  - jobs/tick shows no data and is limited to one run per 15 s.
- **Black-box on localhost as the demo Sunrise teacher:** pages for a Day One Test School student (profile and fee ledger) return 404, and search returns nothing from the other school.

**Not covered:** the admin and principal demo logins need a two-step code that only appears in the server log, so I did not test school-admin flows black-box. The scratch scripts I used are in D:/all/Projects/School-OS/qa-output/security/ (rls-check.mjs, rls-db.cjs, rls-db2.cjs, fns.cjs, ids.cjs, signin.cjs, bb1.cjs, xff.cjs).

verdicts.why:
The code does what the finding says, but the blueprint asks for this behaviour, so it is not a bug in the build.

Code: loginGrantRefusal (src/lib/staff/login-ceiling.ts:73-84) refuses only isTopRole roles (School Admin, Principal, or any role whose settings mark is not none) and exceptions that are for Settings or above the giver's own level. giveLogin (src/lib/staff/staff.ts:283) calls only that check. The Add Staff and staff profile pages (add/page.tsx:90, [staffId]/page.tsx:274) hide only the top roles. So an HR-template login (Staff & HR Full, no Settings) can give the Accountant or Vice Principal role.

Why it is not a vulnerability as written:
(1) docs/blueprint/modules/09-staff-hr-management.md says Add Staff is used by the HR role template (line 9). Step 2 has the person 'Pick one or more roles (for example Teacher, Class Teacher, Accountant, Librarian)' (line 89), and the Role record is edited there ('assigns roles to the staff login', line 352). The blueprint wants HR to give the Accountant role to new hires, even though HR has no Fee access.
(2) The file's header comment (lines 5-9) states the rule as only top roles, Settings exceptions and exceptions above the giver's own. The 'above' message is used only for exceptions. The code matches that rule.
(3) Every login created this way writes an audit entry and calls alertPermissionChange, which alerts every School Admin.
(4) The earlier audit already reported this exact gap as an open owner decision. run-3/REPORT.md:184 says roles other than top roles are not compared with the giver's access, so HR can give Accountant, and that this 'matches the rule stated in commit 7323433f... the owner should confirm which is meant'. That is not a new defect.

The 'made-up staff member' scenario is a trusted HR person misusing a power the blueprint gives them on purpose. School Admins are alerted and an audit trail is kept. It is not an authentication bypass or a hidden escalation. Whether HR should be limited to roles inside its own access is a product decision that is still open (L5). If the owner chooses the stricter rule, the suggested fix is sound. Until then this is hardening, not a confirmed high.

I confirmed this from the code. I did not run it against localhost, because that would have reset a real local user's password, and the code path is clear without it.

1. **The check skips the target's roles.** `signInLinkRefusal` (src/lib/staff/login-ceiling.ts:90-99) refuses only in four cases:
   - the target holds a top role (School Admin, Principal, or any role that opens Settings) that the giver does not hold;
   - the target has a personal exception the giver could not give;
   - the login also opens another school;
   - the giver can change Settings, Users & Permissions (then nothing is refused).
   It never compares the target's other roles with the giver's own access. Yet its refusal text `LOGIN_CEILING_WORDS.linkAbove` says "or more access than yours".

2. **The HR role can reach it.** The HR template has Staff & HR Full, so it passes `who(fd, true)` (`viewer.change === "all"`). It has no Settings access.

3. **The link reaches the HR person's browser.** `newSignInLink` (staff-hr-management/[staffId]/actions.ts:193-208) calls `issueInvite`, which returns `{ link: "/invite/<token>" }`. The action returns `{ link, username, sent }`, and `act()` (src/lib/staff/act.ts:47-54) passes it back as `data`.

4. **The token alone sets a new password.** `acceptInvite` (src/lib/auth/invites.ts:45-69) needs only the token. It sets the password and clears lockouts.

5. **Most targets have no two-step code.** Vice Principal, Office Staff, Exam In-charge, Academic Head, Teacher and Librarian all have `requiresTwoStep` false in roles.ts. For them the new password alone signs the HR person in as that person. Accountant targets are blocked by the two-step code, which goes to the victim.

Where it is weaker than claimed:
- Run-3 already listed this as part of open lead L5 ("needs validation, owner decision"). It is a known gap, not a new one.
- `loginGrantRefusal` also has no role ceiling below the top roles. HR could already give a Vice Principal role to a new staff login it creates, so HR can already get that much access by another route.
- What this adds is taking over a specific person's existing account. HR then acts under that person's name in the audit log and sees their own-scope data.
- The victim's password changes, an invite message is sent and the audit log records "invite-link-made", so the takeover is noticeable.
- HR and Vice Principal are templates that each school must switch on first.

Even so, a lower-access role taking over higher-access accounts, against the code's own stated rule, is a real privilege escalation inside a school.

I could not confirm the claimed impact. I confirmed this by reading the code. I did not run it against localhost:3000, because that needs a campus-limited School Admin set up in a school with two or more campuses.

1. accessAction (src/app/(school)/settings/users/actions.ts:85-98) takes userId, roleIds, scope and campusId straight from the form. The only check is runSettings('users','edit').
2. That leads to requireSettingsAction (src/lib/settings/page-access.ts:65). It checks only the Settings module reach, refuses only page mode 'view' or reach 'own', and never looks at current.campusId.
3. changeAccess (src/lib/settings/users.ts:182-226) then calls checkScope (lines 80-88). checkScope only checks that the scope is a known value and that a CAMPUS campus exists.
4. changeAccess has no `userLoginId === ctx.userId` refusal. disableUser has one (line 261) and resetTwoStep has one (line 320). Editing your own access is allowed on purpose: person-forms.tsx says "Your own access changes straight away." It also has no check comparing the new scope with the actor's own campus limit.
5. So a campus-limited admin who posts scope=WHOLE_SCHOOL for their own id gets the old SchoolAccess row archived and a new WHOLE_SCHOOL row created. Only the scope changed, so no sign-out happens, and keepOneAdmin passes because they are still an admin.
6. On the next request, accessIn (src/lib/auth/access.ts:117-129) picks the widest scope and sets campusId to null, so every campusFilter stops applying. The scope picker in the UI (access-fields.tsx:55) even shows the "Whole school" option, so no form tampering is needed.
7. inviteUser (users.ts:115-121) goes through the same checkScope, so a campus-limited person can also invite a new whole-school School Admin login.

Why this is a real hole and not a design choice:
- The project already holds campus-limited Settings users to their campus. Whole-school data export is refused when current.campusId is set (settings/data-security/actions.ts:27, exports/[id]/route.ts:21, data-export.ts:94). The page says "Only someone who works for the whole school can export all school data."
- Commit 8777bb36 kept campus-limited School Admins to their campus in Document Designs and Privacy.
- One form post gets around all of those fixes. 20-settings.md:69 says a one-campus person changes only their campus "everywhere ... every action". The rubric calls this privilege escalation inside a school, so high.

Precondition: the actor must be limited to one campus and have Settings edit reach 'all' with the Users page in full mode, for example a School Admin role with scope One campus.
